notes.0-3: 'As he stood at the window, something struck him' can be read as being hit by an object or as a thought occurring to him.

notes.0-2: 'He made his pitch' or 'the pitch was perfect' fits a thrown ball or a sales talk.
notes.0-3: 'Her pitch was perfect' fits a thrown ball or a musical tone.
notes.2-3: 'She got the pitch just right' fits a sales talk or a tone of voice.
notes.3-4: 'Its pitch was higher than expected' fits a note's tone or a roof's steepness ('high-pitched roof').

notes.0-2: 'His pitch was perfect' fits a tone of voice or a throw.
notes.0-3: 'The pitch was higher than expected' fits a voice's tone or a roof's slope.
notes.0-4: 'His pitch was too aggressive' fits a tone of voice or a persuasive speech.
notes.1-2: 'The pitch was unplayable' (cricket) fits the playing field or the bowled delivery.
notes.2-4: 'He delivered the pitch' fits a throw (delivery) or a persuasive speech.

notes.1-2: 'From the boat they watched the low bank on the horizon' fits a fog/cloud bank or a river's edge.
notes.2-4: 'She walked down to the bank' is the classic ambiguity between a riverside and a financial firm.
